newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies media Cosby murder transcripts.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies media Cosby murder transcripts.

text.p: A judge ruled on Friday that transcripts of the grand jury proceedings in the murder of entertainer Bill Cosby's son should remain sealed to ensure the accused killer's right to a fair trial.
Superior Court Judge John Reid refused a request by several news organisations for the documents to be unsealed.

Releasing the transcripts "would be a denial of the defendant's right to a fair trial," Reid said, adding that publicising the grand jury proceedings would make it more difficult to seat an impartial jury in the case.
On Tuesday, Mikhail Markhasev, an 18-year-old Ukrainian immigrant, pleaded not guilty to murdering Ennis Cosby in January.
Markhasev was arraigned in Reid's court on one charge of murder with special circumstances, which could carry the death penalty, and another charge of attempted robbery.
Reid gave the prosecution until May 30 to decide whether to pursue the death penalty in the event Markhasev was found guilty, and set a hearing on the matter for that date.
In Friday's ruling on unsealing grand jury documents, Reid hit out at the media which had argued that by not releasing the transcripts, it would have to rely on unsubstantiated rumours.
"I can't control that if there's no professional responsibility in the press -- that's their fault," Reid said.
Cosby, 27, a graduate student, was killed by a single bullet as he was changing a flat tyre near the fashionable Bel Air section of Los Angeles in the early hours of January 16.
